namedUncreditedSkips.name: 10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-05 / SPK-04 — the internal image and the sandbox, in-cluster AC-2b [ED-05, SPK-04, Platform/SRE] — the same pod spec APPLIED, with Chromium’s sandbox observed active in-cluster: non-root under the cluster PodSecurity level, unprivileged user namespaces on the nodes, launch logs showing the sandbox active with no disabling flag, /dev/shm sized sufficiently, and a controlled-fixture run producing a readable webm from that pod. CARRIES story 10.12 AC-6b. There is NO fallback that disables the sandbox: if neither RuntimeDefault nor a Platform-approved Localhost profile works, this escalates to Platform/SRE and Security. Closes when docs/qa/spikes/SPK-04/ carries the evidence and ED-05 is updated.

ADR-001 open item O-4. The chart renders RuntimeDefault as a deliberate starting value, never inherited from the backend and never Unconfined.

CARRIES story 10.12 AC-6b with AC-2b.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-04 / SPK-05 — egress enforcement and destination policy AC-8b [ED-04, SPK-05, Platform/SRE + an unnamed application owner] — enforcement proven FROM a runner pod with the policy applied: approved host reachable; unapproved host blocked; REDIRECT to an unapproved host blocked; subresources and authentication-provider hops to approved hosts allowed; cloud/cluster metadata and control endpoints, link-local ranges and local files unreachable; DNS behaviour for an unapproved name recorded; callback and object store reachable. If the spike finds only static L3/L4 policy exists, §9.3 requires that per-run destination checks in the runner become the PRIMARY control and that Security accept that limitation EXPLICITLY — that acceptance, or its absence, is part of this criterion’s evidence.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-04 / SPK-05 — egress enforcement and destination policy AC-9b [ED-04, ADR-002 O-6, @architect then the implementing story] — story 10.17’s destination-misuse negative tests, un-skipped against the enforced mechanism. The gate-shut tripwire over the production ACCEPTED_JOB_KEYS is re-run UNCHANGED and green in test/run/canary.test.ts; adding a policy field to the closed RunJob is ADR-002 Class B and no story may land it before an architect rules.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-13b [ED-06, SPK-02 question 3, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — TWO TIMED execution.snapshot EVENTS REACH A REAL BROWSER SEPARATELY, before response closure, through every proxy layer, captured as a HAR from a real browser on the staging hosts. The DEPLOYMENT half is done and asserted over the rendered manifest: a separate Ingress carrying only the two streaming paths, proxy-buffering off, and an idle timeout derived from the stream lifetime and compared against the rendered heartbeat in the same manifest. What is deferred is whether any of that survives the wire. A PASSING BACKEND TEST IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS CRITERION and must not be offered as one — the SSE assessment says so directly: "a buffered mock-controller response does not prove SSE delivery". Closes when docs/qa/spikes/SPK-02/ carries the HAR and ED-06 is updated.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-14 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 4, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — a 15 s HEARTBEAT KEEPS AN IDLE STREAM OPEN across the ingress and any platform proxy, and the EFFECTIVE MAXIMUM STREAM LIFETIME is measured against the intended 60 s. If the effective maximum is BELOW the configured lifetime, the configured value moves to match the measurement and the change is recorded — studioSse.lifetimeSeconds is a §8.5 starting value, not a commitment, and the ingress timeout is derived from it so it moves too. That is the mechanism working, not a criterion failing. Nothing in this repository can measure a proxy it has never crossed.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-15 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 5, Platform/SRE (ingress) + backend dev] — RECONNECT WITH Last-Event-ID TO A DIFFERENT API REPLICA restores the current snapshot. The evidence must show the two connections were served by DIFFERENT PODS: a reconnect that happens to land on the same replica proves nothing and is the way this criterion gets reported passed without being tested. Production runs three replicas scaling to six. The design answers this by reading committed state rather than by affinity, and **NO STICKY-SESSION OR SESSION-AFFINITY SETTING MAY BE INTRODUCED TO MAKE IT PASS** — story 10.18b introduced none, and the streaming Ingress it added carries no affinity annotation of any kind. Trading a design property for a deployment workaround would close this criterion by defeating the thing it exists to check.

The DEPLOYMENT half is done: exact-origin credentialed CORS compared against the rendered frontend host in the same manifest, never a wildcard, and no credential in any URL. A DEMONSTRATED GATEWAY INCOMPATIBILITY IS A VALID OUTCOME — it selects the documented GET fallback and changes no execution contract.
